text: Quicksort is a comparison-based sorting algorithm. On average it runs in O(n log n) time. It sorts in place and is not stable.
Mergesort is a sorting algorithm with O(n log n) time complexity. It is stable but not in place, since it needs extra space to merge.
Bubble sort is a simple comparison-based sorting algorithm that runs in O(n^2) time. It is stable.
Insertion sort is a sorting algorithm. It runs in O(n^2) time in the worst case. It is stable and operates in place.
Heapsort is a comparison-based sorting algorithm running in O(n log n) time. It sorts in place but is not stable.
Selection sort is a sorting algorithm with O(n^2) running time. It sorts in place and is not stable.
Binary search is a search algorithm that finds an element in a sorted array in O(log n) time.
Linear search is a search algorithm that scans each element in turn, running in O(n) time.
A stack is an abstract data type that follows last-in, first-out (LIFO) ordering.
A queue is an abstract data type with first-in, first-out (FIFO) behavior.
A binary search tree is a data structure in which each node has at most two children, kept ordered for search.
A red-black tree is a kind of binary search tree that stays balanced through node-recoloring rules.
An AVL tree is a self-balancing binary search tree.
Counting sort is a sorting algorithm that runs in O(n) time. It is stable.
A deque, or double-ended queue, is an abstract data type that allows insertion and removal at both ends.
